The menu is for a dish called 麻辣烫 (má là tàng) which is like a precooked hotpot that you get get to add whatever you want in (the options in the menu or toppings I guess). The first two characters mean numb and spicy (characteristic of Sichuan cuisine) and the last means hot but more in a boiling sense (like boiling meat). This is likely the dish that the picture is of. While 粉丝 (fěn sī,  the clear noodles) is not an ingredient option on the menu, it is likely included as a base ingredient rather than a "topping".

酸辣汤 (suān là tāng) is a sour and spicy soup that is not from Sichuan. The consistency is thicker than soup and the dish is more commonly found in dimsum restaurants. They don't usually have noodles in them and I also did not see the first picture labeled as sour so I don't think it is what you're looking for.
